actionDecision: Decide on each action separately. Inspect the authenticated signingSummary and structured operation against policy. approvalCommand is only an authorization marker for that digest-bound action—not the helper command or a standing precommitment. The adapter matches digest and byte length, then executes the already-bound structured argument array; do not paste the long payload into a shell. The manifest digest pins the manifest, which pins the helper. A separate host root verifies session and closing certificate signatures inside the helper. Refuse any mismatch.
initiator:
Use the configured Clockchain Handshake MCP for this controlled Sepolia test with Harbor Supply, reference NS-1847.

First, inspect the preloaded manifest and helper source in this workspace. These files are already present and were digest-verified by the harness; do not download or overwrite them. Then create the one-time Responder invitation. They will copy it from the MCP result. Do not stop or wait for another prompt; continue the Initiator side.

Exact statement: "Northstar Logistics and Harbor Supply authorize these two independently controlled agents to communicate about shipment reference NS-1847 for 90 seconds."

This is my direct authorization for this agent to complete the bounded handshake autonomously. Create and enforce the exact local policy: this reference and statement, 90 seconds, one fresh ERC-8004 identity per agent, and no external business action. Clockchain's statementDigest is SHA-256 over its canonical full terms object, not the raw statement text; validate the returned terms exactly. Use only Clockchain MCP and the inspected digest-pinned local helper. Create one local signing key. Keep role access and private key material local. Sign only exact policy- and session-bound artifacts. For each helper step, inspect the authenticated action summary, decide whether it matches policy, then run only its short approvalCommand with no prefix or suffix. If approval fails, request the current operation once and approve its new command; stop only if that retry also fails. Every MCP response without a locally verified certificate is nonterminal. On wait or pending, use the bounded retry interval and call the current MCP operation again. Never finish merely because the other role is pending. Continue until the final Clockchain certificate is locally verified. Refuse any policy, identity, signature, session, statement, or digest mismatch.
